info.title: SecondChance API
info.summary: Deterministic benefits matching with plain-language explanations.
info.description:
An AI benefits navigator for New Jersey and Rutgers.

Someone describes their situation in their own words. The API extracts a
structured profile, retrieves curated real assistance programs, runs a
**deterministic** eligibility engine over them, and returns plain-language
explanations with an action plan of official links.

### Rules this API guarantees

* **The rule engine decides, the model only words.** A match status is produced
  by deterministic rules over the profile and an approved rule set. No model
  output can create, change or influence a status.
* **Three statuses, and none of them says "eligible".** `POTENTIAL_MATCH`,
  `MORE_INFO_NEEDED`, `UNLIKELY_MATCH`. Only the program that runs it can
  decide eligibility, so this API never claims to.
* **Missing information never disqualifies anyone.** An unresolvable
  requirement produces `MORE_INFO_NEEDED` and names the field it was missing.
* **Nothing is fabricated.** Every program, requirement and citation traces to
  a stored official source with the date it was last checked. Unverified data
  is marked as such and excluded from eligibility claims.
* **We never ask for an SSN, banking credentials, or anything a program does
  not need.** There is nowhere in the schema to put one.
* **Personal content is never logged.** Narratives, income, emails and raw user
  ids do not appear in logs, metrics labels or audit rows.

### Conventions

* Every non-2xx response has the same body: `{"error": {code, message, detail,
  request_id}}`. `code` is stable and safe to branch on; `message` is plain
  language and safe to show a user verbatim.
* Long work is never held open on a request. `POST /api/v1/workflows` returns
  `202` with a run id; poll `GET /api/v1/workflows/{run_id}`.
* A resource belonging to another user returns `404`, not `403`.
* Identity comes from the bearer token. A user id in a body or query string is
  ignored.

post.summary: Extract a structured profile from a description
post.description:
Reads a free-text description of someone's situation and returns the structured profile it determines, the fields it could not determine, and up to five questions whose answers would change which programs are suggested.

Extraction only: no programs are retrieved and no eligibility is assessed, so this answers in roughly one model call. The only side effect is that the profile is saved as a new version.

Nothing is guessed. A field the description does not determine is returned as unknown rather than inferred, and a low-confidence reading is discarded instead of being passed to the rule engine.

post.description:
Starts a full check in the background and returns immediately with a durable run id and the URL to poll. No request is ever held open for a model-backed workflow.

**Idempotency.** Send `idempotency_key` in the body or an `Idempotency-Key` header. Replaying the same key returns the original run with `deduplicated: true` instead of starting a second one. Reusing a key with a different description is a 409 - returning the first run's results would answer a question the user did not ask.

get.description:
The full state of a run: status, phase, a plain-language progress message, a determinate progress fraction, and every result produced so far.

Safe and useful at every point in the run. Matches appear as soon as the rule engine has produced them, before any wording exists; the plan appears when it is built; clarification questions appear only while the status is `AWAITING_INPUT`; and a failure arrives as a plain-language error with the partial results still attached.

A run belonging to another user is a 404, not a 403, so this endpoint cannot be used to confirm that an id exists.

post.summary: Answer a paused check and continue it
post.description:
Supplies answers to the questions a paused run asked and lets it continue from its checkpoint - possibly in a different process, and possibly days later, with nothing re-typed.

An empty `answers` list is a real answer meaning 'continue with what you have'. The unanswered fields stay unknown and the programs they block stay at `MORE_INFO_NEEDED`, which is the honest outcome.

A run that is not waiting for an answer is a 409.

post.description:
Applies an edit to the profile behind an earlier run and re-evaluates it. **Deterministic and synchronous**: the rule engine decides every status and no model is called, so the returned run is already complete and the first poll has results.

Only the programs whose rules could actually read a changed field are re-evaluated. Every other match is carried forward with the wording the user has already read, so correcting household size neither re-bills twenty explanations nor changes twenty sentences underneath them.

post.summary: Ask a question about a program
post.description:
Answers a question from official sources only.

The response separates `facts` - each traceable to a cited source - from `interpretation`, which is the assistant's reading and is labelled as such. `is_grounded` is computed, not supplied: it is true only when at least one citation survived verification, and when it is false `ungrounded_notice` is populated so the interface has no way to render an unsourced answer as if it were official.

`run_id` and `program_id` only scope which sources are searched. Neither is trusted as authorisation, and a run id the caller does not own is ignored rather than rejected.

Permanently removes every row belonging to the authenticated user: profiles, runs, matches, plans, steps, audit events and the workflow checkpoints that hold what they wrote.

One transaction, so either all of it is gone or none of it is. The response is a receipt with the row counts that were deleted and a statement of what was kept and why.

Result of ``DELETE /api/v1/account/data``.

A privacy promise has to be verifiable, so the user gets counts of what was
actually removed. ``retained`` names what deliberately survives and why -
currently only aggregate, non-identifying telemetry rows whose user
reference has been nulled.

ActionItemPatch.title: ActionItemPatch
ActionItemPatch.description:
Body of ``PATCH /api/v1/action-items/{id}``.

Only completion is editable. Titles, URLs and deduplication come from the
plan generator, so a user cannot rewrite an item into a link somewhere else.

ActionPlan.title: ActionPlan
ActionPlan.description:
The persisted plan for one workflow run.

Versioned rather than mutated: editing a profile and re-running produces
version N+1, so a user can see what changed and a completed step is never
silently rewritten underneath them.

official_name.title: Official Name
official_name.description: The program's name exactly as the administering body writes it.

administering_org.title: Administering Org
administering_org.description: Who actually runs it. Shown next to the name so the user can see SecondChance is not the provider.

description.title: Description
description.description: Factual description, close to the official wording.

plain_language_summary.title: Plain Language Summary
plain_language_summary.description: One or two sentences at roughly a 6th-grade reading level.

who_it_helps.title: Who It Helps
who_it_helps.description: Short audience bullets, e.g. 'Households with children'.

official_url.title: Official Url
official_url.description: The program's own official information page.

application_url.title: Application Url
application_url.description: Direct application entry point, when one is published.

keywords.description: Lexical retrieval aids. Not shown to users.

last_verified_at.title: Last Verified At
last_verified_at.description: When a human last checked this record against the sources.

active_rule_version.title: Active Rule Version
active_rule_version.description: Version of the approved rule set in force. ``None`` = unrated.

ChatMessage.title: ChatMessage
ChatMessage.description:
One prior turn, replayed by the client.

History is client-supplied and therefore untrusted: the prompt builder must
treat it as data and never as instructions.

program_id.title: Program Id
program_id.description: Scopes retrieval to one program's sources.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: Scopes the answer to a run the caller owns. Ownership is checked server-side; the id in the body is never trusted as authorisation.

answer.title: Answer
answer.description: The full answer, in plain language.

facts.title: Facts
facts.description: Cited claims. Each one is traceable to a source.

interpretation.title: Interpretation
interpretation.description: Uncited reasoning, rendered under an explicit 'our reading' heading.

is_grounded.title: Is Grounded
is_grounded.description: Computed, not supplied: true only when citations exist.

ungrounded_notice.title: Ungrounded Notice
ungrounded_notice.description: Computed. Populated exactly when is_grounded is false.

excerpt.title: Excerpt
excerpt.description: Verbatim passage supporting the claim. Must appear in the cited source.

Citation.title: Citation
Citation.description: A pointer into an official source document.

ClarificationAnswer.title: ClarificationAnswer
ClarificationAnswer.description:
One answer submitted when resuming a paused run.

``skipped`` is a real answer, not a missing one: it tells the workflow to
record the field as unknown and stop asking, which is how a user gets
results without surrendering information they would rather not share.

ClarificationInputKind.title: ClarificationInputKind
ClarificationInputKind.description: The control the frontend should render for a clarification question.

value.title: Value
value.description: Machine value submitted back in the answer.

label.title: Label
label.description: Plain-language label shown to the user.

help_text.title: Help Text
help_text.description: Optional one-line clarification of the option.

ClarificationOption.title: ClarificationOption
ClarificationOption.description: One choice for a select-style clarification question.

field.title: Field
field.description: The profile field this question resolves.

question.title: Question
question.description: The question, in plain language, at roughly a 6th-grade reading level.

why_it_matters.title: Why It Matters
why_it_matters.description: What this answer would change, in the user's terms.

affected_program_ids.title: Affected Program Ids
affected_program_ids.description: Programs whose status could change. Empty means profile-wide.

is_required.title: Is Required
is_required.description: Questions are skippable by default. Skipping records the field as unknown and leaves affected programs at MORE_INFO_NEEDED.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: Unit label for numeric input, e.g. "people".

ClarificationQuestion.title: ClarificationQuestion
ClarificationQuestion.description:
A question asked only because the answer could change the results.

``why_it_matters`` is required. If an author cannot say what the answer
would change, the question should not be asked - that requirement is what
keeps the clarification step from turning into a government form.

profile_fields_used.title: Profile Fields Used
profile_fields_used.description: Profile fields actually read, for auditability.

threshold_applied.title: Threshold Applied
threshold_applied.description: The concrete threshold used, in plain language, e.g. "130% of the 2026 federal poverty level for a household of 4".

missing_fields.title: Missing Fields
missing_fields.description: Fields whose absence caused an UNKNOWN outcome.

children.title: Children
children.description: Child evidence for all_of / any_of / not.

ConditionEvidence.title: ConditionEvidence
ConditionEvidence.description:
The audit record of evaluating one condition.

Stored with the evaluation so that an assessment made months ago can still
be explained: which rule ran, which profile fields it read, what threshold
it applied, what it concluded and which official source justified it.
``children`` mirrors the condition tree for combinators, so the reasoning
is inspectable rather than collapsed into one boolean.

ConfidenceLevel.title: ConfidenceLevel
ConfidenceLevel.description:
Coarse confidence band shown to users.

Deliberately coarse: a numeric score implies a calibration this system does
not have.

note.title: Note
note.description: Short operator-facing note, e.g. "model access not provisioned". Never an upstream exception message.

DependencyStatus.title: DependencyStatus
DependencyStatus.description: One dependency's reachability. Carries no error detail.

rule_version.title: Rule Version
rule_version.description: Version of the rule set that produced this result. Never 'latest'.

score.title: Score
score.description: Ranking aid only, in [0,1]. Combines how much of the rule set resolved definitively with retrieval relevance. It never affects ``status`` and is not a probability of eligibility.

missing_fields.title: Missing Fields
missing_fields.description: Union of missing_fields across the evidence tree.

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.description: Known gaps in this assessment: requirements the engine cannot evaluate, stale sources, conflicting guidance. Always surfaced to the user alongside the status.

EligibilityEvaluation.title: EligibilityEvaluation
EligibilityEvaluation.description:
One deterministic assessment of one program for one profile.

Reproducible by construction: given the same profile, the same
``rule_version`` and the same FPL table, re-running the engine must produce
an identical record apart from ``evaluated_at``.

message.title: Message
message.description: Plain-language, user-safe explanation. Safe to render verbatim.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Optional structured, user-safe context, for example {"field": "household_size"}. Never contains personal content, upstream exception text or stack traces.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Correlation id for this request. Quote it when reporting a problem.

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail
ErrorDetail.description: The inner object of the error envelope.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: The body of every non-2xx API response: ``{"error": {...}}``.

source_ids.title: Source Ids
source_ids.description: At least one. A fact with no source is an interpretation.

FactStatement.title: FactStatement
FactStatement.description: A sentence presented as fact. Cannot exist without a citation.

label.title: Label
label.description: Plain-language scope, e.g. "All of New Jersey".

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description: Liveness. Static by design - no dependency is consulted.

HouseholdComposition.title: HouseholdComposition
HouseholdComposition.description:
Who is in the household, as counts rather than people.

Counts only - no names, no dates of birth. Programs define "household"
differently (SNAP counts people who buy and prepare food together; a tax
credit counts dependents), so each count is stored separately and each rule
states which definition it applies in its own ``household_definition``.

IncomePeriod.title: IncomePeriod
IncomePeriod.description:
The period an income figure was reported for.

There is no ``UNKNOWN`` member on purpose. An income amount without a known
period cannot be normalised, so the unknown case is modelled by leaving
``income_period`` unset - and ``UserProfile`` rejects an amount without one
rather than assuming monthly.

narrative.title: Narrative
narrative.description: The user's description of their situation, in their own words.

prefilled.description: Structured answers the user gave directly.

IntakeRequest.title: IntakeRequest
IntakeRequest.description:
What the user submits on the onboarding screen.

The narrative is free text in the user's own words. Pre-filled fields come
from the optional structured questions shown alongside it, and always win
over the same field extracted from the narrative.

unknown_fields.title: Unknown Fields
unknown_fields.description: Fields the narrative did not determine.

clarification_questions.title: Clarification Questions
clarification_questions.description: Questions whose answers could change which programs are suggested.

ambiguities.title: Ambiguities
ambiguities.description: Statements that could be read more than one way.

extraction_source.title: Extraction Source
extraction_source.description: Whether the live model, a cached response or the deterministic path ran.

IntakeResponse.title: IntakeResponse
IntakeResponse.description:
Result of ``POST /api/v1/intake``: what we understood, before any run.

Extraction only - no retrieval, no eligibility, no model-written prose - so
it returns in roughly one model call. It exists so the onboarding screen can
show "here is what we understood, is this right?" and let the user correct
it before committing to a full run. Confirming cheap mistakes up front is
far better than explaining expensive ones afterwards.

headline.title: Headline
headline.description: One short sentence. Must not contain 'eligible' or 'ineligible'.

why_it_may_fit.title: Why It May Fit
why_it_may_fit.description: Reasons drawn only from evidence with outcome TRUE.

what_we_still_need.title: What We Still Need
what_we_still_need.description: One line per missing field, phrased as a question.

caveats.title: Caveats
caveats.description: Limitations copied from the evaluation. Never softened or dropped.

MatchExplanation.title: MatchExplanation
MatchExplanation.description:
Plain-language wording for a status that has already been decided.

The generator is given the status and the evidence and asked only to word
them. ``generated_by`` records which path produced the text, so a run that
fell back to deterministic templates (no model access, a timeout, or output
that failed validation) is visibly different from one that did not.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: The run whose profile is being edited.

changes.description: Fields the user changed. ``None`` means unchanged.

MatchRequest.title: MatchRequest
MatchRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /api/v1/matches``: re-evaluate after a profile edit.

Starts a new run that reuses the source run's profile with ``changes``
applied, and re-evaluates only the programs whose rules actually read a
changed field (see
:meth:`app.schemas.contracts.EligibilityEngine.affected_programs`).
Unaffected matches and their explanations are copied forward, so editing
household size does not re-bill every program's explanation.

MatchStatus.title: MatchStatus
MatchStatus.description:
The only three verdicts this product may ever express.

"Eligible" and "ineligible" are determinations only the administering
agency can make. SecondChance reports a preliminary assessment, so the
vocabulary is deliberately hedged and these three values are exhaustive.

NeedCategory.title: NeedCategory
NeedCategory.description:
What the user said they need, in their own framing.

Kept separate from :class:`ProgramCategory` because a need is a statement
about a person and a category is a property of a program; the mapping
between them is many-to-many and lives in
:data:`NEED_TO_PROGRAM_CATEGORIES`.

total.title: Total
total.description: Total rows matching the filter, ignoring the window.

total.title: Total
total.description: Total rows matching the filter, ignoring the window.

total.description: Total rows matching the filter, ignoring the window.

ProfileDraft.title: ProfileDraft
ProfileDraft.description:
An all-optional patch over a :class:`UserProfile`.

Used for pre-filled intake answers and for the "edit my information"
screen. Validated on its own so the client gets field-level errors, then
merged by ``app.services.profile_assembly`` which owns the precedence
policy. ``None`` means "no opinion"; it never clears a known value.

ProfileFlag.title: ProfileFlag
ProfileFlag.description:
Closed set of boolean profile facts a rule may test.

A flag is only ever set from something the user stated explicitly. Nothing
here is inferred: a narrative mentioning a child does not set
``HAS_CHILDREN``; it produces a clarification question instead. Keeping the
set closed is what makes that reviewable, and it keeps the extraction
model's structured output constrained to names the rule engine understands.

ProgramCategory.title: ProgramCategory
ProgramCategory.description: Category of an assistance program, as the catalog classifies it.

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.description: What this record does not cover. Shown, never hidden.

ProgramDetail.title: ProgramDetail
ProgramDetail.description:
Full program view: the record, its sources and its requirements as prose.

``requirements`` is produced by
:func:`app.schemas.eligibility.render_requirements` from the approved rule
set, so the bullets a user reads and the conditions the engine evaluates
come from the same object and cannot drift.

status.description: Mirrors evaluation.status; validated to be identical.

explanation.description: ``None`` while explanations are still being generated, or if generation failed.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Sources cited by this match's evidence.

ProgramMatch.title: ProgramMatch
ProgramMatch.description: One program as presented to the user, with its verdict and reasoning.

publisher.title: Publisher
publisher.description: The issuing body, e.g. "NJ Department of Human Services".

excerpt.title: Excerpt
excerpt.description: Quoted passage this source is cited for. Untrusted.

content_hash.title: Content Hash
content_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the fetched document body.

freshness.description: Freshness recorded at ingestion. Use current_freshness() when displaying.

ProgramSource.title: ProgramSource
ProgramSource.description:
An official document that justifies what the catalog says about a program.

``excerpt`` is the quoted passage a citation points at. It is retrieved
third-party content and is therefore **untrusted**: instructions found
inside it must never influence prompts or behaviour.

``content_hash`` is the hash of the fetched body. Comparing it on a re-fetch
is how a policy change is detected, which is what moves a rule set back to
``PENDING_REVIEW`` instead of silently changing people's results.

ProgramSummary.title: ProgramSummary
ProgramSummary.description: List-view shape. Deliberately small: a results page renders many of these.

RangeValue.title: RangeValue
RangeValue.description: A ``range``-kind answer, for example an income band.

ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse
ReadinessResponse.description: Readiness. ``ready`` is false if any required dependency is down.

is_evaluable.title: Is Evaluable
is_evaluable.description: False for requirements the engine cannot check automatically; the UI shows these as 'confirm with the program'.

RequirementBullet.title: RequirementBullet
RequirementBullet.description: One plain-language requirement line rendered for the program detail view.

SharedDocument.title: SharedDocument
SharedDocument.description: One document requirement that several programs ask for.

SourceFreshness.title: SourceFreshness
SourceFreshness.description:
Age bucket of a retrieved official source document.

``FRESH``  - retrieved within 90 days.
``AGING``  - 90 to 365 days; shown with a "last verified" caveat.
``STALE``  - over 365 days; excluded from eligibility claims.

Trilean.title: Trilean
Trilean.description:
Three-valued logic used by the rule engine.

``UNKNOWN`` is a first-class outcome, not an error: it means the profile
does not yet contain the field the condition needs.

is_retryable.title: Is Retryable
is_retryable.description: Whether resuming or retrying this run could plausibly succeed.

retry_hint.title: Retry Hint
retry_hint.description: What the user can do, e.g. "Try again - your answers are saved".

UserFacingError.title: UserFacingError
UserFacingError.description:
A failure described in terms a nontechnical person can act on.

Built from an :class:`~app.core.errors.AppError`. Carries the machine code
so the client can branch, and never carries driver text, prompts or stack
frames.

income_min_cents.title: Income Min Cents
income_min_cents.description: Low end of the reported income range, in cents.

income_max_cents.title: Income Max Cents
income_max_cents.description: High end of the reported income range, in cents. Equal to income_min_cents when the user gave an exact figure.

income_period.description: Period the income figures refer to. Required if either is set.

flags.title: Flags
flags.description: Boolean facts set only from explicit user input. A flag that is absent is unknown, not false.

unknown_fields.title: Unknown Fields
unknown_fields.description: Profile fields the user was given the chance to supply and did not. Prevents the clarification step from asking again.

extras.title: Extras
extras.description: Non-eligibility context captured for wording only, for example a preferred language. Never read by the rule engine.

UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description:
The sanitised, validated profile the rule engine evaluates against.

Every field is optional because a profile is built incrementally - from a
narrative, then from clarification answers - and must be evaluable at any
point. Absence means "not known", never "not applicable".

VerificationStatus.title: VerificationStatus
VerificationStatus.description:
How much a catalog record has been checked by a human.

Only ``VERIFIED`` records may support an eligibility claim. ``UNVERIFIED``
records are shown as informational leads with an explicit label, which is
how the product honours "never fabricate a requirement".

WorkflowCreateRequest.title: WorkflowCreateRequest
WorkflowCreateRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /api/v1/workflows``.

``idempotency_key`` is how a double-tapped submit button or a retried
request stops producing two runs and two plans. The server stores the key
per user and returns the original run.

poll_url.title: Poll Url
poll_url.description: Relative URL the client should poll.

deduplicated.title: Deduplicated
deduplicated.description: True when an idempotency_key matched an existing run and no new run was made.

WorkflowCreateResponse.title: WorkflowCreateResponse
WorkflowCreateResponse.description: Immediate ``202`` response: the durable id to poll.

WorkflowPhase.title: WorkflowPhase
WorkflowPhase.description:
One member per LangGraph node, used to drive user-facing progress.

The member names mirror the graph node names exactly so a node can report
its own phase without a lookup table. Users never see these strings - see
``app.schemas.workflow.PHASE_PROGRESS_MESSAGES`` for the copy.

WorkflowResumeRequest.title: WorkflowResumeRequest
WorkflowResumeRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/resume``.

An empty ``answers`` list is valid and means "continue with what you have":
the run proceeds and the unanswered fields stay unknown, leaving affected
programs at ``MORE_INFO_NEEDED``.

profile.description: What we currently understand, for the 'edit this' affordance.

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.description: Run-level caveats, e.g. a stale source or a program with no encoded rules.

WorkflowRunDetail.title: WorkflowRunDetail
WorkflowRunDetail.description:
Full run view. Safe and useful at every point in the run.

Partial-result contract:

* ``matches`` fills in as soon as the engine finishes, before explanations.
* ``plan`` stays ``None`` until the plan node completes.
* ``clarification_questions`` is non-empty only while
  ``status is AWAITING_INPUT``.
* ``error`` is set only on ``FAILED``, and results gathered before the
  failure are still returned, so a late failure degrades rather than
  discards.

WorkflowRunSummary.title: WorkflowRunSummary
WorkflowRunSummary.description: List-view shape for a user's run history.

WorkflowStatus.title: WorkflowStatus
WorkflowStatus.description:
Lifecycle of one workflow run.

``AWAITING_INPUT``  - parked on a LangGraph interrupt, resumable by the user.
``INTERRUPTED``     - the process died mid-run; resumable from the last
                      checkpoint without re-asking the user anything.
``FAILED``          - terminal, carries a user-safe error.
